rule: The Sending Analyzer sees ONE logical key however many physical keys feed it (an on-screen key, a MIDI/Vail key's paddles, the keyboard). Each source is either held or not. The logical key is down while ANY source is held: it goes down when the first source goes down, and up only when the last held source is released. A step's result is the new logical state when this step changed it ('down' or 'up'), otherwise null. A key-down from a source that is already held changes nothing; a key-up from a source that is not held changes nothing. 'releaseAll' drops every held source at once (the input was switched away, a key was unplugged) and reports 'up' if the logical key was down, otherwise null.

cases.name: two sources overlap, first pressed is released first
two sources overlap, last pressed is released first
a release that overlaps the next press never opens the key
a repeated key-down from the same source changes nothing, and one release still opens it
a key-up with nothing held changes nothing
a key-up from a source that is not held does not release the others
three sources, released in a different order
two separate bursts stay two bursts
releaseAll while down reports up once, then everything starts clean
releaseAll with nothing held reports nothing
